To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inhibition of purified lysosomal phospholipes A1 by DH is mixed in nature, that drug binding to phospholipase-substrate complexes is important in the observed inhibition, and that DH binding to phosphatidylcholesterol is not involved in the observed inhibition.
the inhibition of lysosome phospholipase by diethylamnioethoxyhexestol is mixed type, and that drug binding to the substrate is an important factor in this inhibition.
the binding of diethylamino-ethoxyhexestrel to small unilamellae vesicles of di-oleoyl-phosphatidyl-choline is a mixed type of binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inhibition of phospholipases by drugs.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of the inhibition of lysosome enzymes by the antineoplastic drug diethylamino-ethoxyhexestrel.
the inhibition of lysosomes phospholipase activity by diethylamonoethoxyhexestrool (DH) and the mechanism of inhibition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

diethylamino-ethoxyhexestril inhibits the lysosomal phospholipes A1 in vitro by binding to the substrate and enzyme, and that hydrolysis of the enzyme-substrates-drug complex occurs at a rate slower than hydrolysis of enzyme substrate complex.

the inhibition of lysosomes by diethylaminoisethoxyhexestol is due to a mixed type inhibition, in which the drug binds to the enzyme and the substrate, and that the inhibition is due to the binding of diethylamino-ethoxyhexestrel to the substrate, and to the binding of the drug to the substrate, respectively.
DH inhibits phospholipase activity by binding to the enzyme and to substrate, the latter being a more important factor than the former.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DH binds to phosphatidyl-choline in a manner which is dependent upon the drug concentration, the lipid phase, and the presence of other lipids.
DH inhibition of lysosomal enzyme activity may be due to both drug-enzyme interaction and drug-substrate interaction.
DH binds to phospholipids and phospholipase in a mixed type of competitive inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inhibition of phospholipase activity by DH may be a result of the interaction between DH and phosphatidyl-choline, and not a direct interaction of DH with the phospholipase itself.
